analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md: the patch adds two table rows at head lines 415-416 (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED). The supplied units are the base excerpt (lines 519-686) and the head excerpt (lines 1-353), which do not include the added rows or the surrounding table. I could not read the new rows as head text and relied on the patch excerpt. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache behavior is modified. The base excerpt covers the SSD prefix cache and memory settings, and the head excerpt covers GLM, endpoint resumption, logout, App Attest worker and model-cache settings. Both are unchanged context.

The documented behavior has a security implication that the next pass should check against the source. With default-on streaming of auto tool calls, `tool_calls` fragments are emitted before the call frame closes. The doc says each call is still validated at frame close. If the provider has already sent fragments to the consumer by then, a malformed or invalid call could be partially disclosed. This stays within the consumer-visible response channel, but the source should be checked for the validation failure path.

The doc says both variables are forwarded to the LaunchAgent, and both are exact-`0` kill switches that default on. This relates to T-008, because streamed chunks must stay encrypted on the coordinator-to-provider leg. That path is not shown here, so I did not conclude anything about it. The implementing files (ToolStreamPreparation.swift, ReasoningPromptProbe.swift) were not supplied. Whether the encryption and fail-closed path covers the new early-streaming code, and whether T-008 needs updating, is unverified. I recorded no finding because there is no evidence of a regression. The docs-only change is low risk, and I request a code-level check only for the unsupplied implementations.
